note: One line per performance round: what it targeted and what it measured. Console figures are from the real PS Vita (444 MHz); Vita3K figures from the calibrated emulator (222/240 MHz, 3 cores).

rows.summary: Scene recorder in the Debug menu (draw lists, assets, timing, pad, sampled pcs), Vita render scale 0.5-2x safe to change live, idle-thread turn.
rows.result: Recordings of the user's fights became the main bug and perf evidence.

rows.summary: Skeleton pose fast path (state in host registers, recursion as a loop); optional plain floats for the lean code (off, not exact).
rows.result: Exact; a few % in Vita3K.

rows.summary: Colossus death mask and tendrils drawn right; no more terrain holes while the area streams in.
rows.result: Missing-terrain frames 212 -> 0 in Vita3K.

rows.summary: Collision natives as plain NEON on the Vita, EntryCollisionFinder native, glEnd no longer waits for the worker.
rows.result: Decomp 5.41% of the code.

rows.summary: Generated code skips clamps it can prove useless (VU0 lanes, FPU results), PS2 adder alignment only where it changes a bit, dead stores dropped.
rows.result: Exact (byte-identical with switches off); ~2% in Vita3K.

rows.summary: Loop back edges store the pc only when a checkpoint is due, float facts kept across joins and loads, register cache across short joins.
rows.result: ~1-2% in Vita3K; console fight 11-13 fps (r23 ~10).

rows.summary: DMA chain walk reads RAM directly, guest-memory slow paths through register-saving trampolines (-13.6% memory instructions in the hottest code), 2D waits off the game thread.
rows.result: ~1-3% in Vita3K.

rows.summary: Found the console profile's modelDisp 16% was a sampler artefact; the real cost was the game thread waiting 4-9 ms a frame for the model worker. Textured 2D and zFog waits removed, leaner modelDisp hook.
rows.result: Console: frame median 60 -> 50 ms, but still hitching.

rows.summary: Logs no longer written to the memory card on the game thread (~5 ms a frame), no eviction churn, game thread alone on a core, worker at higher priority.
rows.result: Console-only problems: Vita3K shows none of them.

rows.summary: The 150-285 ms hitches were card writes of debug lines: all stderr now buffered. Skinned pass deferred to the worker, mesh pools compacted.
rows.result: Exact (30M late reads checked, 0 changed).

rows.summary: 26 MB more GPU pool headroom (vitaGL's 32 MB circular pool used at most 65 KB a frame), shared scratch depth buffers, skeleton 8-10% fewer instructions.
rows.result: Console: frames over 100 ms 174 -> 11; game thread still 50-62 ms of pure CPU.

rows.summary: Canyon walls fixed (heap-pressure eviction no longer drops meshes stored in the GPU pools; the console had evicted 25,772 in one session). 30 fps cap always on the Vita, but only in frames that draw a scene, so loads stay fast. Fewer particles in the Debug menu. Area-change bursts spread over frames.
rows.result: Sacrifices saved under 1 ms: the game thread is game logic (collision, Wander and Agro, camera). Next: native rewrites of camera collision.

rows.summary: GS vs native: untextured colours were drawn twice as bright (the whole picture was washed out), Wander and Agro ground shadows added, vertex fog matched to the GS, F9 flips GS/native live on the Mac.
rows.result: Mean brightness gap native vs GS +8..+10 levels -> about 0. Open: far landscape, Agro mane alpha, altar stones, some glows.

rows.summary: Far landscape drawn with the depth test like the GS (the grey blocks and white shapes on the horizon). Shadows work on the real Vita (the targets had no stencil buffer) and are on by default, with half the vertices. The GS alpha test in every shader.
rows.result: Horizon matches the GS at every camera position checked. Body shadows cost about 1.3 ms in Vita3K.

rows.summary: Camera collision check rewritten as native code: the camera wrappers, the segment matrix chain, the camera's object and id filters, and the shared vertex fetcher. Exact: 538,800 difftest checks, 0 mismatches.
rows.result: About 0.7% of the game thread; decomp 5.59% of the code, 49% of calls. The rest of the camera module is spread over ~100 small functions.

rows.summary: The scripts' collision callback, the wall judge (44,500 calls on the route), the plane lookup and the water probes rewritten as native code. Difftest now checks every native, not just the first 64; no old native had a hidden mismatch.
rows.result: About 0.35% of the game thread; decomp 5.73% of the code, 45.1% of the game thread native.

rows.summary: 27 of the hottest recompiled functions rewritten as native code: the animation system (motion matrices, interpolation, IK without the IK step), character geometry, the gaze, ambient light, pad history, cloth tension, and a cluster of character-control functions. Exact: 97,700 checks, 0 mismatches.
rows.result: About 3.3% of the game thread. Decomp 7.49% of the code, 51% of calls; 52% of the game thread now runs native.

rows.summary: Native-to-native calls made cheap (the guest call path inlined: ~20 instructions a call instead of ~45), 20 more natives (sprites, display-list layers, layout classes, collision work flush, motion frames, microcode transfer, camera context), 421 redundant VU clamps dropped. Exact.
rows.result: About 4% of the game thread between both changes; 56% of the game thread now native, 54% of calls.

rows.summary: Tail jumps in the generated code now go through the function table, so natives are used by every caller. 13 more natives: reflections, the slope probe, small-animal AI, the stage object manager, the camera record, layout lights, the IK step and more. Semaphore signals without the syscall overhead when nobody waits.
rows.result: 60% of the game thread native, decomp 8.66% of the code. Open: check the slope probe on the Vita.

rows.summary: Console regression in r42 traced to the body-shadow volumes being rebuilt every frame on the worker: rebuilt once and reused, half the worker's work. A/B rotation for the console to price every feature. 15 more natives, including the rest of the collision keep test and gsReg.
rows.result: Console r42: game thread 54 -> 69 ms, worker 8 -> 40 ms vs r35. Fix measured only in Vita3K so far (worker -50%).

rows.summary: Console A/B priced every feature: the natives save ~23 ms a frame against the recompiled code; body shadows cost 4.5 ms, the alpha test 3.2. All kept on and made cheaper: depth/stencil memory traffic cut from 26 to 10 MB a frame, fewer full-size copies, merged alpha-test passes, lighter shadow volumes.
rows.result: Console r44: game thread 49 ms on the plain (r35: 54, r42: 69). Colossus fight still GPU-bound (present 60-94 ms).

rows.summary: 30 more natives: foot IK, Agro's body step, control checks, sword blur, leg IK, texture transfer records, and fight-heavy collision, animation and particle functions found in the user's fight recordings.
rows.result: Game thread -3.1% (Vita3K); 64.7% native, decomp 10.9% of the code. One native (010CABA0) still has a rare one-byte mismatch.

rows.summary: Found why one native differed by one byte: while a native called guest code, its caller's saved registers were still in place, and a callee copied a stack slot holding one into a new object. Natives now keep the original's saved registers across calls; fixed the same pattern in character geometry. 24 more natives (life bar, particles, expressions, VRAM allocator and more).
rows.result: Exact again (0 in 50,200 checks at every call). 67% of the game thread native, decomp 11.7% of the code, 58% of calls.

rows.summary: The script system (scripts are compiled MIPS coroutines woken every frame) and the object lifetime rewritten as native code, with a coroutine framework so a script can sleep and resume in either native or recompiled code. Every native audited for the saved-register leak: none left.
rows.result: 69.5% of the game thread native, decomp 12.7% of the code, 65% of calls. Per function the natives now cost what the lean code did: next comes making the native code itself faster.

rows.summary: The hottest natives made faster than a transcription on the Vita's Cortex-A9 (host pointers, values in locals, plain NEON where the PS2 clamps provably change nothing) behind SOTC_FASTNATIVE; fresh-setup boot fix (module relocation stays recompiled until GAMECORE runs).
rows.result: Exact: Mac difftest 0 mismatches; Vita3K compared every A32 fast path at every call, 0 mismatches in 16.2 M checks. Vita3K A/B: game thread -5% (indication; console A/B pending).

rows.summary: The thread switch's C++ unwind on the Vita: the unwinder's table lookup answered from a checked cache of return addresses (libgcc's __gnu_Unwind_Find_exidx).
rows.result: Exact (0 mismatches in 590 k checked lookups, 99.97% cached); small: ~95 lookups a frame.

rows.summary: The Vita's smear while the camera moves: cameraBlur's screenBlur fires on nearly every moving frame at 16-20 fps, 98% of the calls the identity; those are left out (the picture they draw is the picture itself), real zoom / shift blurs drawn as before.
rows.result: Vita3K attract demo: frames drawing a screen blur 454 of 3 706 -> 7 of 3 982 (each also a full scene redraw saved); Mac Metal / GL native vs GS unchanged (RMSE 0.072 -> 0.069, 0.058 -> 0.056).

rows.summary: The EE scheduler's thread switch (a WaitSema / SleepThread that blocks, a SignalSema that wakes a higher thread: ~400 a second) made by returning through the generated code instead of throwing a C++ exception, which on the Vita is a full ARM EHABI unwind; host frames that go on after guest code rethrow at their level as before (PS2X_XFER_RETURN).
rows.result: Same state either way (Mac audit mode over the attract demo, the new-game intro and a save load / save screen: no frame went on). Vita3K 240 MHz A/B: game thread 23.45 -> 23.12 ms (-1.4%).

rows.summary: The keyboard state the game reads every frame (256 keys, no keyboard attached) read with host pointers and written once a key when the caller's words lie apart from it (SOTC_FASTNATIVE2, a new switch for the next fast paths). Also tried and reverted: a lighter wait for the sound mixer's lock.
rows.result: Exact (difftest 0 mismatches; random-state test 0 differences). kbGetStatus 0.42% -> 0.03% of the Vita3K game thread (~0.08 ms a frame). The mixer change cut the game thread's lock wait 10% but cost the frame 2 ms: not kept.

rows.summary: The wind zones' walk (~45 calls a frame over 80 mostly empty slots) skips the empty slots in a tight loop and moves its sorted records inline instead of through a library memmove (SOTC_FASTNATIVE2).
rows.result: Exact (difftest 121 600 checks, 0 mismatches). Vita3K 240 MHz: the walk's own share 1.16% -> 0.23% of the game thread; rounds 53-54 A/B: game thread 23.39 -> 22.98 ms.

rows.summary: Vita3K's red canyon mist: the GS backend's start-up probe left a red 64 x 64 surface in memory vitaGL freed, and Vita3K sampled the next texture put there (often the mist's puff) as that surface; the probe no longer runs in an emulator and freed targets are kept there. The real camera blurs are drawn on a second picture instead of from the scene drawn again (SOTC_SBLUR_PINGPONG). vitaGL takes the PS2's own mip levels.
rows.result: Mist red in about 4 Vita3K runs of 10 before (7 of 7 red runs with the puff in one of the two freed blocks; with the probe's bands made green the mist came out green), 0 of 8 after. Blur: no scene redraw; Vita3K A/B with every camera blur drawn: render thread 23.2 -> 22.4 ms; frame 59.3 -> 63.3 ms, all of it in Vita3K's present (console not measured).

rows.summary: vitaGL's per-draw work made lighter on the Vita: a packed draw's attributes on one vertex stream (one sceGxmSetVertexStream instead of 4-6), the default uniform buffers copied with memcpy instead of the sceClibMemcpy import, a 16-entry vertex layout cache (SOTC_GL_LEAN_DRAW). Found that Vita3K stalls ~1 s every ~90 frames while the Mac's screen is locked (host present), which had skewed the 60-frame averages.
rows.result: Vita3K attract demo, stalls left out: render thread 20.8 -> 18.9 ms at 222 MHz (-9%), 16.2 -> 14.5 ms at 300 MHz; frame 34.7 -> 34.1 ms at 222, 32.7 -> 32.1 at 300. Not 30 fps: the title screen's world runs ~42 ms at 222 (game thread ~35 ms).

rows.summary: vitaGL's glUniform copies (the skinned palettes, up to 3 KB a call) use the library memcpy instead of the sceClibMemcpy import, under SOTC_GL_LEAN_DRAW; planFrame's draw compare unrolled. A draw-pass range search was measured and dropped (no effect).
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz A/B (rounds 56+57 together): render thread 20.2 -> 18.1 ms, frame 34.5 -> 33.6 ms; the title screen's world 44.9 -> 40.0 ms (game thread ~33 ms there). Not 30 fps yet.

rows.summary: Game thread: the heap garbage pass keeps its time check while no guest code ran and the EE clock has not moved (~400 checks a frame skipped), the collision finder's duplicate search over host memory, the model hook's scroll rows kept per plan a frame (SOTC_FASTNATIVE3, checked: 0 differences). The A/B runs' own cost cut: abSwitches no longer builds strings every frame (~1.3% of the game thread), and SOTC_AUDIO_LOG=0 in measuring runs.
rows.result: Vita3K A/B: game thread 22.5 -> 21.2 ms at 222 MHz, 17.1 -> 16.6 ms at 300 MHz (at the edge of the noise); frames at 2 vblanks 81% at 222 (84% of the attract demo's first 7 000 frames, ~51% in the title screen's world), 90% at 300. Not 30 fps yet.

rows.summary: The camera blur hook's wait for the hook worker only when it records a blur (SOTC_SBLUR_JOIN=0, opt-in): it removed ~95% of those waits but measured no frame-time gain, so the old join stays the default. Found that Vita3K's per-frame vblank count jitters (31 ms frames counted as 3 vblanks): slips are now counted as frames over 40 ms (slips.py).
rows.result: Frames over 40 ms on the attract demo: 300 MHz ~3% (title screen's world 2-8%), close to a held 30; 222 MHz ~8-9% of the first 7 000 frames (half game thread, half ~1 950-draw render frames) and ~60% of the title screen's world (game thread ~41 ms). Not 30 fps at 222.

rows.summary: The frame's display list (the VIF1 DMA chain) is walked on a worker thread, as the PS2's DMA ran beside the EE: the kick hands it over and leaves the channel busy; its effects (VIF1 registers, the GS SIGNAL / FINISH / LABEL writes, MSKPATH3, the channel's completion and the GS interrupt) are applied on the game thread where the game could first see them (SOTC_DMA_ASYNC, default on). Checked: every chain's result and every byte it reads compared with a walk at the kick, 0 differences on the Mac and in Vita3K.
rows.result: Vita3K A/B: game thread -1.9 ms (attract demo) / -1.7 ms (title screen's world) at 222 MHz, -1.6 / -1.7 ms at 300 MHz; frames over 40 ms in the title screen's world at 222 MHz 30.5% against 48.8%. Not 30 fps at 222 yet.

rows.summary: The game's model display state (modelDispState: the part tree's camera tests, the layers' last surface, the shadow flag) runs on a thread of its own with the hook's part decision; the model jobs wait for it, and the VU0 CLIP register stays pending until a reader needs it (the box tests before each model record their judgements, every other reader joins). Checked at every hook against the old code on the same state, 0 differences on the Mac and in Vita3K (SOTC_MDS_LANE, default on).
rows.result: Vita3K A/B (game thread + hooks): -0.8 ms (attract demo) / -1.6 ms (title screen's world) at 222 MHz, -0.6 / -1.2 ms at 300 MHz; frames over 40 ms in the title screen's world at 222 MHz 30.5% against 46.6%. Not 30 fps at 222 yet.

rows.summary: The particle geodisps' per-frame clip pass and the small functions every particle pass asks (the geodisp class, the emitter list) natively, checked against the recompiled code (0 mismatches in 272 700 checks); the kernel snapshot for the debug panel made only when asked; the 30 fps cap back in the Vita's Quality menu (on by default then, off by default since round 64; a saved choice honoured).
rows.result: Vita3K A/B: within the noise at 222 and 300 MHz (the functions were ~0.8% of the game thread). After rounds 60-62 the title screen's world at 222 MHz still slips about one frame in three; not 30 fps at 222 yet.

rows.summary: The collision queries counted for the first time (a census of every query the game makes per frame): in the title screen's world ~800 distinct small queries a frame from ~40 call sites, ~5 ms in Vita3K at 222 MHz, almost none repeated, so no single structure to replace. The collision leaf now tests the surface's plane first and skips the id filter and the full surface test for surfaces the segment does not cross, checked both ways (3 million checks, 0 differences; Mac difftest 0 mismatches).
rows.result: Vita3K A/B: game thread -0.6 to -0.8 ms in the attract demo's first part at 222 and 300 MHz; no change beyond the noise in the title screen's world, where the character's finders and keeps dominate. Not 30 fps at 222 yet.

rows.summary: The first subsystem moved to the Vita's other cores: the frame's texture animation loop (each animated texture's scroll and palette, ~310 textures) runs on a new offload thread and is joined before its first reader. A census tool on the Mac (every guest load of the loop's output watched) found who reads it and when: nothing before the display walk. Checked both ways on the Mac and in Vita3K (11 300 frames, 0 differences, 0 reads in flight). The 30 fps cap in the Vita's Quality menu is off by default now, as the user asked.
rows.result: Vita3K A/B: game thread -0.5 to -1.0 ms in the attract demo's first part at 222 and 300 MHz; within the noise in the heavy part (the loop was ~1.5% of the game thread). The other candidates (particles, cloth, wind) share state with the rest of the frame and are each under 1 ms. Not 30 fps at 222 yet.

rows.summary: Performance cuts the player chooses, in the Vita's Quality menu (Select twice), all off by default and saved: fewer camera checks (the camera's look and visibility tests every other frame; the test that keeps it out of walls still every frame), distant characters at half rate (the pose of a character far from the camera every other frame), effects at half rate (particles stepped every other frame with both frames' time) and a shorter draw distance (models the game already lets vanish go at 2/3 of their range), plus a Max performance row that turns all four on. With all of them off the game runs as before (Mac difftest of the touched functions: 0 mismatches beyond the known noise).
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz, pooled A/B runs: effects at half rate saves ~2 ms of the game thread; the camera checks, the draw distance and the distant characters 0.2-1 ms each; all four together ~0.8-1.8 ms of the game thread (frames over 40 ms in the heavy part 24% against 26%). Useful in particle- and camera-heavy places, far from the ~20 ms a locked 30 fps on the console needs.

rows.summary: The Vita build's code layout, for the console's Cortex-A9 (small caches and TLBs) rather than Vita3K: every function in its own section and the 3 934 functions Vita3K profiles sampled linked hottest first at the start of the code, with vitaGL and the C libraries right after them. The 90% hot set now fits in ~2 MB instead of being spread over 34 MB (4 KB pages it touches 745 -> 530, 64 KB pages 146 -> 41). The guest RAM is page aligned (it was 8-byte aligned, so half of the 16-byte guest loads crossed two cache lines). Sized and not done: -Os for cold code (only 13% smaller), splitting cold blocks out of functions (GCC cannot with ARM exceptions), and a generator change for the remaining codegen overhead (the recompiled code is ~18% of the game thread now).
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz A/B (two runs each): the same within the noise, as expected (Vita3K does not model the console's caches). The effect can only show on the console: an estimate of 0.5-2 ms of the ~56 ms heavy frames, more if the Vita maps the code with large pages. A console profile run (SOTC_SUBSYS_PROF) is prepared.

rows.summary: For the console's DRAM latency (~250 ns a miss, no useful hardware prefetch on the Cortex-A9): the walks that touch every object's records once a frame on the game thread now ask for their lines ahead (SOTC_WALK67, on by default, switchable in one console run with SOTC_AB_FLAG=walk67): the display walk's objects 3 ahead with its own lines, the sort lists in stages, the part matrices and the GIF packet; the model hook's texture scroll chains level by level; the cloth grid in one block; the particle draw 4 particles ahead; the collision leaf's boundary records and the work flush. Only reads and prefetches: difftest exact. A Mac-side proxy (SOTC_LINES67) counts the cache lines each walk touches and how many were not asked for in time.
rows.result: Mac proxy: the same distinct lines (the game's records), the exposed ones (likely console misses) down 55-61%: heavy part 3 257 -> 1 260 a frame, early 2 659 -> 1 211. Vita3K 222 MHz (which cannot show cache effects): the added reads cost ~0.2-0.5 ms of the game thread in light parts, heavy part within noise. Estimated on the console: ~0.25-0.5 ms; the prepared console A/B will tell.

rows.summary: The bloom, haze and redraw artefacts on the Vita compared with the PS2's GS stage by stage, the same frame logged on both sides: the blur taps now modulated by the temporal alpha as the GS does (the 64 x 64 history was 8-20% too bright, so the sky out of the shrine went white); the title's blur taps made branchless (Vita3K skipped them); the shrine's openings cut at the game's own layer-1 near plane with per-surface vertex fog; Vita3K's white streaks on Agro and Wander traced to the mid-frame redraw, now off by default; particles no longer write depth, so the sky's haze is masked as on the GS.
rows.result: With the modulated taps the GS's integer model of the blur reproduces the GS buffer exactly (100% of the pixels, two frames); the white sky out of the shrine and Vita3K's white streaks are gone; cloak and fades checked along the Load Game route. Picture only, no speed change.

rows.summary: Where the shrine's frame goes: the game thread everywhere (the render thread never waited on); at the altar 18 characters' geometry a frame (the doves and lizards), collision ~13 ms over ~50 query sites, the display walk. The walk's prefetch records are now deduplicated through a 64-slot hash instead of comparing every line pair (SOTC_PREF69; same prefetches in the same order).
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz, in-run A/B at the altar: game thread -1.6 / -1.7 ms (two runs) of ~60 ms; walking out of the shrine 55.1 -> 52.9 ms, the plain 38.5 -> 37.2 ms.

rows.summary: The characters' geometry measured callee by callee with probes only on a chosen list (SOTC_SUBSYS_PROF_ONLY): every callee above 0.4 ms is already native; a third of the 18 ms is collision under the walkers' root dynamics. A cloth mesh fast path was tried (exact, no gain, dropped). The console's game-thread waits are split by site in the frame log (| waits), and thread priority / core knobs added (SOTC_THREAD_PRIO, SOTC_THREAD_CORES).
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz with the console's settings: the altar 61.3 ms a frame (game thread 59.2), the plain 38.1 (37.0). On the console the game thread waits 12.6 ms a frame (Vita3K ~1): the next console run names the site.

rows.summary: The walkers' collision at the shrine's altar (Wander's and the lizards' root dynamics, ~6 ms of the game thread in Vita3K): the slide's and the landing's finder filters native and called without guest round trips (manager_sub_010DF8F0, slideExceptionJudgeCB's attribute lookup), ClipCollisionFinderWithKeep native, the finder's duplicate search from the newest entry (70% of the surfaces that reach it are already in the finder), the finder leaf's plane distance on NEON. SOTC_COLL71, on by default, switchable with SOTC_AB_FLAG=coll71.
rows.result: Exact: Vita3K fast-path checks 4.4 M, 0 mismatches; difftest on the Mac and in Vita3K, 0 mismatches. Vita3K 222 MHz in-run A/B at the altar: game thread -1.00 / -0.18 / -0.50 ms (three runs, ~60 ms frames; the root dynamics' probes -0.54 ms); the plain unchanged. The finder leaf (~2 ms) and the finder clips (~2.5 ms) are the next pieces.

rows.summary: The console's ~12 ms a frame of the game thread waiting at the shrine (the frame log's hookjoin) turned out to be round 61's modelDispState lane, not the hook worker's model jobs: the lane (priority 191 on cores 1-2) gets a core only after the hook worker, audio and the render thread, so the game thread slept at the layer cache's and the CLIP register's joins. Now the lane's jobs are run by whoever holds their token, always the oldest first: a join of the game thread runs the jobs left itself, and the hook worker runs the ones its models need (SOTC_LANE_HELP, on by default, switchable in one console run with SOTC_AB_FLAG=lanehelp).
rows.result: Exact: SOTC_LANE_HELP_CHECK compares each job's results at the hand-over with its real run: 0 of ~1.2 M on the Mac and 0 of 67 000 in Vita3K (with the help off, a late lane differs in 1-2 jobs per 157 000: the help makes jobs run sooner). Vita3K hides the wait (~1 ms); with the lane held 100 us a job to mimic the console, hookjoin 9.1 -> 0.3 ms and the game thread -3.3 ms; in plain Vita3K the game thread is 0.4-1.1 ms slower (it runs ~22 jobs a frame itself). Console A/B prepared (expected ~7-10 ms off the shrine's 74 ms frame).

rows.summary: The console's heavy frames are now bound by the GPU (present ~30 ms a frame, the render thread busy the whole frame). Fewer GPU scenes a frame with the same pixels (SOTC_GL_FEW_SCENES, on by default, A/B scenes73): the picture is shown as drawn (two pictures in turn) instead of copied for the host, the glow layer is drawn at the soft shadows' break so the darkening and the glow's composite share one scene of the picture, and the picture's last scene no longer stores its depth. Textures uploaded in GXM's swizzled layout (SOTC_GL_SWIZZLE, on; SOTC_GL_SWIZZLE_BOTH=1 makes it switchable per frame, A/B swizzle73). Plain texture reads for one-level textures tried and kept off (SOTC_GL_PLAIN_READS). New: SOTC_GL_FREEZE (a still frame for A/B window captures), SOTC_VGL_PARAM_KB, and the frame log's present / targets / scenes / verts columns.
rows.result: Exact: with the altar's frame frozen and the A/B rotating, every Vita3K capture of scenes73 / swizzle73 on and off is the same picture (46 and 36 captures); the plain reads came out 1 level apart on 0.6% of the pixels, so they stay off. The altar: 37 -> 35 GPU scenes, 36 -> 34 target binds, depth / stencil 12.3 -> 9.0 MB a frame. Vita3K hides GPU time (render thread unchanged within noise); console A/B prepared (env-console.txt).

rows.summary: The render thread's own work per draw, with the same GL calls in the same order. Each pass now walks only the drawn draws of its layers instead of every draw of the frame (~7 passes at the altar), the frame's draws are ordered by counting and planFrame compares floats as bits first (SOTC_GL_LEAN_PASS, on, A/B pass74). vitaGL's vertex layout cache now survives vertex buffer switches, which re-patched the vertex program ~170 times a frame (SOTC_GL_KEEP_LAYOUT, on, A/B layout74). A render-thread priority experiment for the console (SOTC_RENDER_PRIO, off, A/B rprio74). New: SOTC_GL_PHASE_LOG (plan / pass / draw-call split of the draw part) and SOTC_GL_MERGE_STATS, which showed ~90% of unmerged neighbours differ in texture, so fewer draws would need reordering and is not exact.
rows.result: Exact: with the altar frozen and the A/B rotating, every Vita3K capture is the same picture (57 and 57 captures). Vita3K route 6, frames with 600+ draws: the render thread's draw part 11.90 -> 10.92 ms and a draw call 16.9 -> 13.5 us; draws per frame unchanged. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, rt74.py).

rows.summary: With r74 the console's heavy frames wait on the GPU (present 35 ms). Two thirds of the GL calls ran a fragment program with discard, which on the Vita's SGX makes each tile wait on the program for visibility. Layer 1's near-plane cut is now skipped for background draws whose mesh bounds lie wholly past that plane (SOTC_GL_FAR_GUARD, on, A/B guard75): 338 of 400 such draws a frame, which then go without discard when their alphas allow. The alpha cut-out is done without discard (pixel drawn with alpha 0, leaving the target unchanged) for draws without depth writes that blend by source alpha into a target whose alpha is kept or unread, in the non-fogged program only, where the shader compiler produces the same arithmetic (SOTC_GL_SOFT_CUT, on, A/B soft75). New: discard counts in the draw log and a [gl:cut] line; rt75.py with a content-matched off-minus-on block.
rows.result: Exact: with a frame frozen and the A/B rotating, every Vita3K capture is the same picture (61 and 61 captures); the fogged variant and a discard-free full program were dropped because the compiler gave them other roundings (1-3 levels on scattered pixels). Discard calls 70% -> 68% of GL calls (no-discard 40% -> 43%): most far background draws still need the alpha cut-out. Vita3K cannot time the GPU; a 32 MB parameter buffer stays off (it would take 16 MB from a CDRAM pool that had 10 MB free on the console). Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, 3 states).

rows.summary: The console's game thread, measured: in the shrine it runs 53-69 ms of CPU a frame (the kernel's run clock, alone on core 0) with only 0.4-2.4 ms of scheduler waits, so it is CPU, not waiting. The frame's order in Vita3K (character tasks ~28 ms, camera 4.4, particles 4.8, display walk ~19, then the frame ends) has no exact parallel split: each step reads what the one before wrote, and the characters share collision bodies, the VU0 random register and guest callbacks. Vita3K's sampler at the altar: collision 23.7% of the game thread, recompiled code 16.7%, the rest below 4.3% each. The frame log's per-frame lines are now formatted on a thread of their own (SOTC_LOG76, on, A/B log76): 0.88 ms a frame of the console's game thread in r74's log.
rows.result: Exact (logging only; the same text, matched by frame number). Vita3K 222 MHz A/B at the altar: log76 -0.5 ms a frame (its log part 0.35 -> 0); the lane off +0.9; the walk prefetch off -2.1 (host caches). Console A/B prepared for the two game-thread switches never measured on the console alone: the modelDispState lane (mdslane; on the console the game thread's joins already run 85% of its jobs) and the walk's prefetch records (walk67). The 30 fps target needs ~half of the game thread's CPU: no exact lever of that size is left at this structure (speculative parallel characters or a frame-behind walk on copies would be rounds of their own; or the opt-in cuts).

rows.summary: The opt-in quality cuts (round 65's camera checks, distant characters, effects at half rate, shorter draw distance; round 36's fewer particles and coarser detail) can now be switched at run time by the A/B rotation, so the console can measure them in one run at the same places: SOTC_AB_FLAG takes sacmax (every cut on outside its windows, all off in them, whatever the saved settings), plus sacptcl / saclod beside the existing per-cut names. Each site was checked to be safe to flip between frames, a [sac] line logs each change, and the settings menu never saves the rotation's state.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz, Load Game -> altar -> plain, 480 s, no crash: all cuts together save 3.7 ms a frame matched by draws (53.1 vs 56.8 ms; frames over 50 ms 70% vs 78%), 4.7 ms in a second run; single cuts are within the noise at ~1 000 frames each. Estimated on the console ~5-7 ms of ~59: not 30 fps. Console A/B prepared (sacmax, soft75: 3 states).

rows.summary: First round under the new rule (a port, not a PS2 copy: same gameplay, no picture loss). The game already updates characters at an interval of its own (ViewIntervalClip gathers the world's time; ExecCharaGeometry and everything under it, collision included, is skipped on in-between frames and the motion advances by the whole gathered time later). Characters the camera cannot see (outside the clip volume this frame and the one before) now wait 0.25 s (birds, lizards) or 0.12 s (Agro) between updates; never the player, anything within 12 of the player, large bodies or the active colossus (SOTC_CHARLOD78, on, A/B charlod78). At the altar Agro alone cost 3-4.6 ms a frame unseen outside the shrine.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz, whole frame matched by draws: altar -5.2 ms (51.8 vs 56.7), plain -5.6 ms (38.7 vs 43.9), attract demo heavy part -1.2 ms. Time handed to put-off characters equals the player's within one interval; attract demo with riding 660 s without a crash; route screenshots show no missing characters. Not checked: climbing a colossus (excluded by design). Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, charlod78).

rows.summary: The display walk measured step by step (~16 ms of work at the altar: group pass 4.2, light pass 2.5, model draws ~5, particle draws 4.1; the profiler's larger means were the host's stalls landing in the frame change). The particle systems were the biggest piece: ~80 tiny systems (fog wisps, feathers) at ~100 us each, all kept by the game's own clip. A Vita-side visibility pass now tests each system's real particle bounds against the camera; a system outside the view is not drawn and its step is put off, with the world's time handed over in one step when it returns or after 0.25 s, so particles keep their speed and ages (SOTC_PTCL79, on, A/B ptcl79 / r79all).
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz whole frame: altar 55.9 -> 50.4 ms (matched by draws -5.8; console env r79all -5.1), out of the shrine and the plain 38.3 -> 31.0 ms, attract demo -0.1..-0.9 ms. Attract demo 660 s with the A/B rotating, no crash; route and attract screenshots on/off show no missing effect. Local-frame emitters (half of the shrine's systems) are not culled yet. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, r79all).

rows.summary: Measured first: Wander alone is 7.4 ms a frame of character geometry even standing still at the altar (root dynamics' collision 4.35, IK 1.7), and the segment tests (camera checks, the player's probes, horse path tests, AI perception: ~14 a frame) ~4 ms; almost none repeats the frame before exactly (idle pose and camera sway move them by millimetres). A segment test now reuses the answer of the same caller's earlier test when both end points are within 1 cm and that answer is at most 5 frames old (SOTC_SEG80, on, A/B seg80 / r80all). A new A/B group `newdir` turns rounds 78-80 off together for the console. Round 79's local-frame particle emitters turned out absent at the altar: nothing to enable. A ground-finder memo was tried and dropped (no gain).
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz whole frame, in-run A/B: altar 46.3 -> 44.8 ms (matched by draws -2.2), route 6 out of the shrine and the plain 30.3 -> 29.2 ms, attract demo unchanged (riding: 7% of tests reused). Rounds 78-80 together at the altar: 58.2 -> 44.8 ms. About half the segment tests reused when walking or standing. Attract demo 660 s without a crash; altar and route 6 screenshots on/off show nothing missing. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, r80all,newdir).

rows.summary: Wander standing still at the altar costs ~4.4 ms of root-dynamics collision a frame. Mapped everything that step writes (a whole-RAM diff), then tried two ways to cut it. First: skip the step while he is at rest. He never quite is: the idle motion moves his root up to ~3 mm a frame. Second: an exact ground patch for the collision finder's leaves, testing only the surfaces near the character. Named the characters around him: his head and Mono's body, head and hair. Their cost is pose, layout and cloth, not collision.
rows.result: Nothing shipped for speed. Vita3K 222 MHz, in-run A/B at the altar: the rest skip gained at best +1.2 ms (below the 2 ms bar), and the ground patch -0.14 ms mean / +0.20 median (exact: wrong 0 on route 6; at the shrine it keeps 88% of the surfaces). Both dropped. Two probes stay, off by default (SOTC_REST81_PROBE, SOTC_REST81_NAMES). Next levers: Wander's pose (IK + GetMotionMatrix, 1.7 ms), the head's and Mono's pose / layout / cloth (~2.7 ms), the ground queries' surviving narrow phase (~3 ms), the render walk.

rows.summary: Profiled the characters' animation at the altar: the pose (GetMotionMatrix) was the largest piece, ~1.5 ms a frame over ~16 calls and ~480 bones, because the code still walked the skeleton the PS2 way (recursion through matrix and quaternion stacks in emulated VU0 memory, every operation clamped). Rewrote the bone pipeline as plain Vita code instead of a translation: the pose as one NEON loop, the layout matrices with no guest calls, the skinning matrices and the cloth mesh's normals on host pointers (SOTC_POSE82, on, A/B pose82 / r82all; newdir now includes it). A check mode compares against the old code: largest pose difference 3e-6.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz whole frame, in-run A/B matched by draws: altar 48.1 -> 46.1 ms (-2.0), route 6 -0.4..-0.7 ms, attract demo riding -1.1 ms; rounds 78-82 together while riding -3.3 ms. Attract demo 660 s without a crash; close-ups of Wander, his head, Mono and Agro on/off show the same picture (no seams). Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, r82all,newdir).

rows.summary: Measured the display walk at the altar: the layout objects' clip cost 2.4 ms a frame (146 objects, 16 us each: a translation with guest calls and every VU0 register kept) and the light pass 2.3 ms (the lights' colour manager, ~85 us an object, remade every frame for objects that do not move under lights that do not change). Redesigned both for the Vita (SOTC_WALK83, on, A/B walk83 / r83all; newdir includes it): each object's light colours are kept and given back while the frame's lights, its light inputs and its position (within 5 cm) stay the same, remade at least every 16 frames; the clip is one host function with NEON products and box test and no guest calls. The particle manager's round trips (SOTC_PTCL83) measured below the bar and left off.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz whole frame, in-run A/B matched by draws: altar 46.1 -> 43.3 ms (-2.8), route 6 -1.5 ms (shrine and plain alike), attract demo -0.5 ms; rounds 78-83 together while riding -3.1 ms. The clip agrees with the old code in 2.1 million checked calls; the light colours differ by a step of 1/255 or more in 21 of 96 000 checked hits (worst ~1.9/255, normals never). Attract demo 660 s without a crash; altar pictures on/off show the same lighting (the route 6 pairs were spoiled by the locked screen; the plain is covered by the check). Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, r83all,newdir).

rows.summary: Profiled the game thread again with rounds 78-83 on: collision is still the largest group at the altar (22.5%), with no function above 3.5%. The largest pieces were Wander's ground step (~5 ms), the particle manager (3.5 ms, a third of it a water search around the camera), the AI path work (2.7 ms, half of it segment tests) and the camera (2.6 ms). Redesigned two world probes that the game redid every frame for answers that change over metres (SOTC_PROBE84, on, A/B probe84 / r84all; newdir includes it): the AI path's visibility tests answered from round 80's memo at path scale (15 cm, up to 10 frames, a pool of their own), and the camera's water search kept while the camera stays within 25 cm (up to 10 frames). A memo of the ground finder's candidates per still object (SOTC_FIND84) measured just below the bar and stays off.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz whole frame, in-run A/B matched by draws: altar 40.8 -> 39.5 ms (-1.2, steady over four runs), route 6 -0.3 ms, the plain and the attract demo unchanged; rounds 78-84 together while riding -2.2 ms. Check mode: the path answers differ from the game's in 0-0.2% of checked tests, the water answers in none of 26 000. Attract demo 660 s twice without a crash; altar pictures on/off the same. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, r84all,newdir).

rows.summary: Measured Wander's ground fill at the altar: ~1.95 ms a frame, nearly all in two still shrine objects whose finder steps enter ~56 surfaces a fill. Redesigned it (SOTC_GROUND85, on, A/B ground85 / r85all; newdir includes it): each still object's step runs once with a grown radius while the leaf records its surfaces (sphere, plane, the tree walk's splits) into host arrays; later fills pick the entries with one host loop while the query stays inside, and the landing / IK finder clips skip candidates the segment cannot reach from the same arrays. Patches are not built at speed (the ride). The AI control LOD for off-screen far creatures was measured (~0.6 ms possible) and dropped: it broke the title flow.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz whole frame, in-run A/B matched by draws: altar +1.03..+1.27 ms in five of six runs (+1.18 on top of round 86), route 6 and the attract demo unchanged within noise; rounds 78-85 riding -3.9 ms. Check mode: 116 668 altar steps, 18 differ by an edge surface; route 6 87 458, 0 differ; no skipped clip candidate was a hit. Behaviour script on/off the same; attract demo 660 s x4 without a crash; two unexplained hangs in ~25 runs did not repeat. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, r85all,newdir).

rows.summary: Found why the game thread waits for the render thread on the console: the hand-over waits until the render thread is idle, and the render thread is busy until its present returns, where vitaGL's swap blocks while the GPU still has the two frames before. So the wait is the GPU's backlog, and the console's frames are either bound by the render side (the shadow-volume frames, render 15.6 + present 23.5 ms) or by the game thread, never both; the run's averages mixed the two. Redesigned the hand-over so the render thread gives the frame's data back before the present (SOTC_GL_PRESENT86, on, A/B present86 / r86all; newdir includes it): the game thread no longer waits for the swap, with the same GL commands in the same order. Added the GPU's own timeline from vitaGL's scene notifications ([gpu86] / [gpu86s], on with the console's frame log) so the next console run names the GPU scenes that make the present.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz, the altar, in-run A/B: unchanged where the game thread is longer (Vita3K's own GPU never makes the swap wait); with a simulated console swap wait, 0.9-1.6 ms a frame faster where the render side is as long as the game thread or longer. Attract demo 660 s with the console env without a crash; altar and route 6 pictures on/off the same, no tearing or old frames. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt, r86all,newdir, GPU timeline on).

rows.summary: The console's run with the GPU timeline showed the GPU is now the limit everywhere (about 62 ms a frame, whatever the game thread does), with the slowest work in the full-size picture scenes. Made the GPU log name each slow scene by what the renderer drew in it, added a per-layer draw summary, and prepared four GPU changes the console can switch on in rotation: fewer frames queued on the GPU (inflight87), the fogged background layer drawn at the size actually used (bgsmall87), shadow volumes counted without a fragment program (vol87), and one picture scene fewer around the altar's soft shadows (shmask87). All four ship off. A sort of the draws by texture to merge more of them was measured slower and stays off.
rows.result: Vita3K cannot time the GPU: the candidates are neutral there, and the 660 s attract demo ran without a crash with them rotating. Pictures: shadows unchanged with vol87, frozen altar frames identical with shmask87, the far scenery within 31 levels with bgsmall87. The draw sort made the render thread 0.9 / 0.55 ms slower (altar / route 6). Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: inflight87, bgsmall87).

rows.summary: Round 87's two GPU wins are now on by default on the Vita: the fogged background layer drawn at the size actually used (bgsmall87) and shadow volumes counted without a fragment program (vol87); inflight87 and shmask87 stay off. Fixed a lost wake-up in the modelDispState lane found by the freeze hunt (a release store followed by a load on the other flag can reorder on ARM; now seq_cst on both sides and a timed wait). Read the console's frame times again: they only looked bimodal because frames over 50 ms are logged on separate 'slow' lines and the title/loading frames at 60 Hz were mixed in; the 3D's frames are one group around 58-61 ms, on whole vblanks, with no pacing waste (GPU busy ~57 of ~58 ms, the game thread ~43-46 ms of CPU). Prepared two GPU changes for the console A/B: world draws whose alpha is provably 1 drawn with blending off, the same pixels but visible to the GPU's hidden surface removal (opaque88), and the water's mirror drawn at 256 x 256, the PS2's own size (mirror88).
rows.result: Console (round 87's eboot, matched in-run A/B): bgsmall87 -5.2 ms a frame (-8.3 on the 3D's frames), vol87 -2.0, inflight87 +3.7, shmask87 0. 3D frames: p50 58-61 ms, 92-100% over 33.3 ms. Vita3K cannot time the GPU; there, opaque88 turns ~107 draws / 45k vertices a frame opaque at the altar (58 / 23k on the plain) with frozen frames identical pixel for pixel, and mirror88 is drawn every frame (also on the plain). Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: opaque88, mirror88).

rows.summary: Profiled the game thread again by subsystem at the altar, on the plain and while riding in the attract demo's world. Since rounds 78-88 no single subsystem is above about 3 ms: the display walk (7-11 ms), the characters' geometry (Wander 2.7-6.4 ms, Agro 3-5 ms when in view), the particle systems (2.4-4.2 ms, mostly Agro's hoof dust while riding: many tiny systems, each paying a fixed per-system cost), the camera, character control and collision. Halving the game thread therefore needs work on other cores. The console's logs show those cores are already 70-85% busy (render thread, audio 10-25 ms, mesh worker 15 ms), and every large block left is game code that cannot yet run off the main thread; that runtime work is written up as the next design step. Shipped two exact particle cuts: the emitters' frame reads the camera, effect name and step kind directly instead of 7-8 game-code calls each (ptcl89), and round 83's per-system round trips are now on by default (ptcl83).
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz in-run A/B matched by draws: ptcl89 -0.11 ms riding / -0.14 altar / -0.21 route 6; ptcl83 -0.16 / -0.23 / -0.42. Attract demo 660 s with the console env, no crash; route 6 pictures on/off show no broken effect. Not 30 fps: the console needs the multi-core redesign. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: ptcl89, ptcl83).

rows.summary: Found where the audio thread's CPU goes on the Vita (10-25 ms of every 60 ms frame on the console): all of it is the sound mixer itself, a fixed per-sample loop for the two mixing cores (routing, the PS2 reverb at 24 kHz on both, master volume) plus a cost per playing voice. Rewrote the mixer to work a block at a time with the same results bit for bit: voices take their samples and envelope levels in runs, the cores sum their routing in simple loops, the reverb steps through pointers instead of wrapping every read, and a reverb whose memory is provably all zero with nothing sent to it is skipped. One deliberate, inaudible change: the PS2 reverb's arithmetic rounds down, so its tail never reaches zero and both reverbs kept running for a residue of 2 parts in 32 768; that residue is now cleared once nothing is sent for a full pass, and the reverb then sleeps. The mixer also takes its lock half as often. Guest RAM page size was investigated and left alone: the 32 MB cannot go into the console's 26 MB of physically contiguous memory (the kind that can get large pages), splitting it is not possible with the system's API, and its page size cannot be measured without the console.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz in-run A/B (all of round 90 off in its windows), the mix per 2 048-frame callback: route 6 4.8 vs 15.1 ms (-68%), the altar 12.0 vs 17.3 (-31%), the attract demo 5.6 vs 12.8 (-57%); the game thread's waits for the mixer's lock about a third of before on route 6 and in the attract demo (81 vs 98 ms per 5 s at the altar); the frame within noise to -1.5 ms in Vita3K. Exactness: the old and new mixer compared on copies in-game (0 differences) and on ~1.7 M random pieces. Listen test: the title music recorded on and off differs by at most 1 LSB over 120 s. Attract demo 660 s with the console env, no crash. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: opaque88, mirror88, r90all).

rows.summary: Looked for what the console's GPU spends its ~50 ms a 3D frame on. The frame time can no longer show GPU savings: the game thread alone takes ~46-52 ms, so a cut in GPU work shows up as GPU idle time, not a faster frame. Read that way, round 88's two GPU candidates both cut the GPU's busy time a lot (12-15 ms) even though the frame did not move, and the render-scale test's GPU time does grow with the pixel count. Added three debug switches for the console's A/B that deliberately break the picture to split the GPU's time: almost no pixels drawn, textures replaced by one texel, and half the vertices sent. Shipped one exact saving (world draws that never read their screen position no longer pass it from the vertex stage) and fixed the live resolution change: vitaGL never freed a render target's stencil memory, so every change leaked a few MB until the GPU memory ran out; a change to a larger picture is now refused when the memory is not there.
rows.result: Vita3K: the frozen altar is identical pixel for pixel with the new vertex program on and off; route 6 with the three diagnostics rotating ran 300 s without a crash; the scale cycle's leaked stencil memory went from 16 MB after six cycles to none, and a forced refusal kept the picture without a crash. GPU timings need the console: env-console.txt rotates diag92px, diag92tex, diag92half (read with ab92.py's split of the GPU's busy time).

rows.summary: Worked on the console's GPU time (~56 ms of busy time a 3D frame). Round 88's two GPU cuts (world draws that cannot be see-through drawn without blending, and the water's mirror drawn at the PS2's 256 x 256) are now on by default on the Vita: the console had measured them at 12 and 15 ms less GPU work. Added three exact savings, on by default: more draws drawn without blending (alpha-tested ones whose pixels are all fully opaque), the mirror skipped in frames where nothing reads it, and the bloom's final full-screen pass made cheaper. Read the GPU programs' compiled sizes: the world's are already short; the outlier is the bloom's blur at ~270 instructions a pixel. Two console candidates that change the picture slightly, off by default: the bloom blur as one weighted sum (its rounding modelled so the glow keeps its strength) and the glow layer's 8-pass blur as 2 passes.
rows.result: Vita3K cannot time the GPU: pictures and stability only. The frozen altar and the frozen plain are identical pixel for pixel with the three exact savings on and off, and with round 88's cuts (one pixel at 1 level). Candidates: the bloom blur brightens the sky's glow ~1 level on average (up to 45 on bright edges), the glow blur within 2 levels. Route 6 300 s with the console env, no crash. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r93all, blur93, glow93), read by GPU busy time with ab93.py.

rows.summary: Built the runtime piece round 89 asked for: recompiled game code can now run on a second CPU core, beside the main game thread. The worker thread has its own copy of the CPU registers, its own stack, scratchpad and matrix stack, and a stand-in for the runtime so it never meets the PS2 kernel's scheduler. It may only run the code it owns (the particle and wind system) and a list of pure maths functions while the game thread runs; anything else (memory allocation, object deletion, collision, character motion) makes it wait until the game thread arrives, after which it finishes alone. Moved the particle systems' per-frame step onto it, running while the display walk sorts the scene; the walk now handles particle objects at the end of its pass. Positions of effects attached to characters (Agro's hoof dust) are asked on the main thread first, and deletions are queued to the end. One crash found and fixed during bring-up. Off by default (not bit-exact: a sub-effect spawned during a step appears one frame later, deletions come later in the frame, particles use their own random-number stream), so the console can A/B it.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz in-run A/B matched by draws, frame time saved with the worker on: attract demo -1.4 ms (riding -1.9), the altar -0.9, route 6 -1.6 (the plain -1.7). While riding the job takes ~3.2 ms on the worker and the main thread still waits ~1.6 ms for it at the walk. 660 s attract runs with the console env (flag rotating): no crash on three builds; stairs, plain walking and riding played; pictures on/off show no missing effect (climbing and a colossus not reached). Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: SOTC_PTCL91=1, opaque88, mirror88, r91all).

rows.summary: Cut the number of GPU scenes a frame (every switch of render target is a scene with a fixed cost on the Vita's tiled GPU; 35 a frame at the altar). The glow layer's 13-step chain became 3 passes, the soft shadows' mask, the glow's first passes and the water's copy now share two targets drawn as regions, the bloom's two blurs share one target, and the background is read where it is drawn instead of copied. Also fixed the background layer reading a stray texture (the bloom's history) in frames without a water mirror. All four new switches ship off: console candidates.
rows.result: Vita3K: the altar 35 -> 17 scenes a frame with all four on; route 6 22.7 -> 15.1 (300 s, no crash). With the bloom off the frozen altar is identical (background), within 1 level (shadows / water) or up to ~22 levels at the screen edge (glow). With the bloom on, the altar's sky glow settled in a different, brighter state whenever any switch was on, although the bloom's mask was identical: the bloom's temporal step can hold several stable states and this could not be pinned down in Vita3K, so they ship off. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r94on, glow94, fx94), read by GPU busy time with ab94.py.

rows.summary: Tried to stop the main game thread from waiting for round 91's particle job on the second core. Three options, all only active when that job is switched on (it stays off by default): the scene's draw walk waits for the particles later (after the lighting pass, or inside the draw loop, drawing late any particle effect whose turn has passed), and, as a console candidate, the particle step starts before the camera instead of after it (it then uses the previous frame's camera for culling). Mid-round the console's verdict on round 91 arrived: on the real Vita the second core made 3D frames ~2.5 ms slower, because the job runs longer there and the game thread still waits for most of it, in one scene from an early point where a dissolve effect sets a particle value. That setter now runs on the worker after the job instead of stopping the game thread, the early start gives the job the camera's time to overlap, and the log now shows how late the worker wakes. Bigger moves (character physics, cloth, camera) were ruled out: they all go through the collision code, which is not safe to run on two cores yet.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz in-run A/B: against round 91 the round's changes give between -0.3 and +1.6 ms depending on the run (riding: the draw-loop join +1.3 alone; the early start +2.6 in one run, -0.5 in another); the worker as a whole still saves 1.2-3.6 ms in Vita3K, which the console contradicts. No crash or fault in 660 s attract runs on three builds, the altar and route 6; one hang found and fixed during bring-up; no pictures (window captures failed). Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: SOTC_PTCL91=1, SOTC_EARLY95=1, r91all, r95all, early95) to decide whether the particle worker pays on the Vita at all.

rows.summary: Measured the game thread again, this time by subsystem: the scene's draw walk, the characters' bodies and the creatures' own scripts are the three largest, and the creatures turned out to cost more than their bodies: Agro, standing unseen outside the shrine, still spent 4 ms a frame on his own logic. Creatures the camera cannot see (small birds and lizards more than 6 units from Wander, Agro more than 12) now run their whole frame only once every 4 frames (Agro every 2); their movement keeps its real speed because the game gives each update the time since the last one, and a creature coming into view is back to every frame within 3 frames. Also reordered the tests of Wander's ground surface selection so the cheap ones come first (exact). A third idea, skipping still characters such as Mono on the altar, was dropped: her pose changes slightly every frame.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz in-run A/B, matched by draws: the unseen-creature cut saves 3.4-5.1 ms a frame at the altar, 2.0-3.5 ms on route 6 and 1.1-3.4 ms riding; the reordered surface tests are within the noise in Vita3K. No crash, fault or hang in 600-660 s runs of the attract demo and route 6 and a 300 s altar run; altar pictures with the cuts on and off match. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: obj96, sel96, r96all).

rows.summary: Went after the Vita GPU's time on the main 3D picture, which the console runs say is mostly spent shading pixels. Vita3K cannot time the GPU, so a new measuring tool estimates, for one frame, how many pixels each kind of draw covers and how many shader instructions each pixel costs. It showed that every textured surface still read its texture the slow way (a texture read computed inside the shader instead of fetched before it starts: an old faster path had been left off because Vita3K draws it one shade apart on a few pixels), that untextured full-screen tints ran the textured program, that the distance fog read the background image for surfaces nearer than where the fog starts (where it changes nothing), and that alpha-tested foliage was shaded twice over its whole area. All of these now take cheaper paths with the same picture, plus a single pass for the glow layer's two full-screen blends. A console diagnostic that leaves one kind of draw out per window was added to measure what each kind really costs on the Vita.
rows.result: Vita3K (no GPU timing): at the frozen altar the estimated shading work drops 45% (197 -> 109 million instruction-pixels a frame; route 6's plain 106 -> 75); pictures identical for most changes, the faster texture reads 1-2 shades apart on ~0.3% of pixels (Vita3K's own rounding), the foliage change up to 5-10 shades on a few hundred pixels; no visible difference side by side. No crash or hang in a 420 s route-6 run with the console settings, the attract demo and six frozen-frame runs. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r98all, diag98, plainread73), read by GPU busy time with ab98.py.

rows.summary: Looked inside the game thread's two biggest blocks, the scene's draw walk and the characters' bodies, with the emulator's sampling profiler, aiming at cuts that change nothing on screen. The time turned out to be spread very thin: no single function is above about 3% of the thread, and with five earlier shortcuts now switched off (they cut Avion's intro short on the console), collision checks are the largest block. Four small exact cuts: a character-link search that scanned the same list twice now scans it once, the AI path-point sort no longer searches the area list again for every point, the model-plan lookup avoids a slow software division, and a ground-surface test runs four at a time (only active when its parent feature is on). Some small math helpers are now inlined.
rows.result: Vita3K 222 MHz: the profiler shows about 0.4% of the game thread saved (~0.2 ms a frame); in-run A/B differences are within the noise (+-1 ms). Check modes for the two search cuts found no difference in 92 000 and 6 million calls. No crash or fault in 600 s attract and route-6 runs and a 300 s altar run; altar pictures with the round on and off match. Exact local rewrites like these cannot reach the 30 ms goal on their own. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r97all, links97, path97).

rows.summary: Went after stutter rather than average speed: every slow 3D frame in the recent console logs (over 1.4x the typical frame) was split by what made it slow. On the latest settings about 10% of 3D frames are spikes. The largest share is the game's own work on its thread (about 44%, round 97's area); then the game waiting for the disc (12%), the GPU running behind (9%; 34-60% in the earlier GPU-heavy runs) and the game waiting for the model-drawing worker at the camera-blur and heap-move points (about 14% together). Four changes, all with the same picture: the camera-blur hook no longer waits for the worker when it draws nothing (nearly always); the GPU is kept at most two frames behind instead of three; the game's disc reads are read ahead in the background so the next request is usually already in memory; and the disc reader threads run above the model worker so the game is not left waiting on them. New readers report p50/p90/p99 and the spike share per A/B state, and the cause table.
rows.result: Vita3K cannot show the console's causes (no worker backlog, no GPU lag): there the switches are within noise once its host stalls are left out, and two 600 s runs of route 6 and a 600 s attract demo had no fault or hang. The read-ahead served 81% of the game's disc reads on route 6. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r100all, sblur100, inflight100), read with tools/ab100.py.

rows.summary: Rewrote the hottest collision code (the game's line-of-sight and ground checks) as plain Vita code that gives exactly the same answers: the walk through each object's collision tree is now a loop that keeps the line in the CPU instead of copying it through emulated stack memory, the matrices used for every surface are prepared once instead of for each surface, and the check against the colossi's and characters' moving surfaces throws out the far ones with one vector test. Each part has its own switch and a check mode that runs the old and the new code side by side.
rows.result: Check modes found no difference in millions of checks across route 6 and the altar, with the round-80/84/85 shortcuts both on and off. Vita3K 222 MHz profiler: collision's share of the game thread falls from 19.0% to 17.0% with the shortcuts off and from 11.0% to 10.1% with them on (roughly 0.4-0.8 ms a frame); in-run A/B differences are within noise (+-1 ms). No crash in 600 s attract (riding) and route-6 runs. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r101all, walk101, skin101).

rows.summary: Looked inside the game's scripts (the creatures' AI and the managers that run every frame) with a new sampler that records which script is running and which game function it is in. The scripts are compiled game code run as lightweight game threads, not an interpreter: the script system's own machinery (switching between scripts, the per-frame script pass, the data-driven AI records) is only about 2.5% of the game thread. The rest of the script time is the creatures' own work (the birds' flight AI, Agro's path, object animations) and the geometry and collision their frames call, spread over hundreds of functions. Two exact changes: the script switch now copies its saved registers with inline vector moves instead of library calls, and the game's text formatting (used by the scripts every frame) no longer builds temporary strings.
rows.result: Check modes compared 3.5 million script switches and 60 000 formatted strings against the old code on route 6 and the altar: no difference. Vita3K profiler at the altar: the copies' share of the game thread falls from 2.4% to 2.1% (about 0.15 ms a frame); the in-run A/B at the altar, route 6 and a 600 s attract demo is within noise (+-1 ms). No crash in the 600 s runs. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r102all, sw102, fmt102).

rows.summary: Looked through the drawing walk for work the game thread still does only because the original fed the PS2's graphics hardware. Two such layers were removed: the particle effects no longer build the PS2's particle packets (and upload its particle microcode) only for the port's renderer to copy their inputs back out; the renderer now gets those inputs directly. And solid models no longer compute per-part matrices for the PS2's vector unit, which nothing in the port reads. Each has its own switch and a check mode.
rows.result: The particle check found the renderer's input byte-identical in 288 000 particle draws (altar and route 6); a test that fills the skipped matrices with invalid values left the picture intact. Vita3K profiler at the altar: the touched code fell from 3.1% to 2.0% of the game thread (about 0.5 ms a frame); in-run A/B +0.3 to +1.4 ms with the round on, within noise. All the PS2-format work left in the drawing path is only about 3% of the game thread; the rest of the walk is its own per-object bookkeeping, which needs a different design rather than more cuts. No crash in 600 s runs. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r103all, ptcl103, solid103).

rows.summary: Tried to run the body work (pose, IK, cloth, ground collision) of characters away from Wander on a second processor core while the game thread goes on with the other creatures' scripts. Built the hand-over and its safety rules: the second core runs the original game code, waits before anything shared (memory allocation, sound, the object lists), and the game thread waits for it before touching the same things; a check mode compares every result with the normal one-core run.
rows.result: Identical results: the check found no difference in 52 characters run side by side and 185 run on the other core alone (altar route). But it is slower, not faster, so it stays off: the characters that can run apart are the cheap ones (birds, Mono's parts, about 3 ms at the altar), the game's shared lists stop them within a fraction of a millisecond, and the other core runs the slower original code. Vita3K A/B: 14.7 ms slower at the altar, 15.2 on route 6, 3.9 riding. No crash in 600 s. Written down for a next try: collision code safe for two cores and the collision lists copied for the second core.

rows.summary: Made room on the Vita's second and third processor cores, where the model-drawing helper thread, the sound mixer and several smaller threads share two cores beside the renderer. The helper thread spent half its time building character shadows, much of it in a slow byte-comparison routine and a slow rounding call; both are now done with faster code that gives exactly the same results. Two threads (the background mesh builder and the renderer) woke up every 2 ms even with nothing to do; they now sleep until they are given work. The timing log's own text formatting no longer uses the slow standard number conversion. Each change has its own switch and a check mode.
rows.result: Check modes compared 14 000 shadow draws (215 MB of model data, 6.5 million shadow vertices) and every log line against the old code: no difference, so the picture is the same. Vita3K profiler at the altar: the helper thread 12% less CPU, the background builder 54% less, the log thread about 75% less; in-run A/B: the helper thread saves 1.8 ms a frame at the altar and 0.6-0.7 ms on the plain. The frame rate in Vita3K is unchanged (the game thread sets it); the idle wake-ups cost far more on the real console than in Vita3K. No crash in 600 s runs or loading a save from the console's memory card. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r105all, worker105, render105).

rows.summary: Added a player option in the settings menu (Select twice, Renderer tab): Frame rate, Auto or Steady 20. Auto is the default and unchanged. Steady 20 makes every picture stay on screen for exactly three screen refreshes (20 fps) in the game's scenes, and starts each game frame exactly 50 ms after the previous one, so the game moves the world by the same step every time and the motion is even instead of alternating between 33, 50 and 67 ms. A frame that takes longer shows at the next refresh, and that picture stays as long as the game's step, so there is no short frame after a long one. Loading screens and menus are not held.
rows.result: Vita3K (own tree, route 6): with Steady 20 the game's step matched the time between frame starts within 2 ms in 99.4% of frames, frame starts 50.05 ms apart (standard deviation 1.1 ms), and in quiet scenes 581-585 of every 600 pictures stayed exactly three refreshes (the rest were Vita3K's own one-second host pauses). Game speed unchanged: Wander's position by game clock followed Auto's along the walk and ended within about 5 units of it. The option saves and loads from settings.cfg; no crash in 600 s runs, including loading the save from the console's memory card. The slow-frame causes that cost little to fix were looked at: the 'blocked' waits are the game waiting for the next refresh, not the disc; the rest belong to other rounds' code.

rows.summary: Went through the game-script work of the birds and lizards, the object animations and the managers that start each frame, to rewrite the hottest pieces as plain Vita code with exactly the same results. Most of what round 102 had listed there was already native code; without its probes the whole area is a few percent of the game thread, spread over dozens of functions. Two real savings: the frame start's pass that keeps attached objects behind their parents now does its many tiny lookups itself instead of calling into the game code for each one (it walked the object list over and over), and the birds' and lizards' search for their flock leader is native. A third rewrite (three object-animation key readers) is exact but turned out no faster than the original code, so it ships switched off. Each has its own switch and a check mode.
rows.result: Check modes compared every call with the original code on the altar, route 6 and the 600 s attract demo: no difference (millions of lookups, tens of thousands of leader searches and animation keys). Vita3K profiler at the altar: the two kept changes take 0.37% off the game thread (about 0.2 ms a frame); the in-run A/B is within its noise. No crash in 600 s runs, including loading the console's own save. Console A/B prepared (env-console.txt: r106all, grp106, ai106).

rows.summary: First step toward running part of the game's main work on the Vita's other cores. Round 104 tried moving far-away characters' body and collision work to a helper thread and found three things in the way. This round removed two of them as groundwork, without changing what the main thread does: the fast collision code now keeps its scratch data separately for each thread, so the helper thread can run the fast code instead of the slow translated code, and the helper thread now walks the game's object lists from a copy taken when it gets the work, so it no longer waits for the game's global lock. The helper path is still off by default.
rows.result: Check mode: 129 comparisons of a character's work done on the helper thread beside the game against the same work done alone, 0 differences. With the helper path on in Vita3K, the fast code on the helper thread saves 6.5-11 ms a frame at the shrine compared with round 104's translated code, but the helper path as a whole still costs 9 ms a frame there and 5.5 ms on the plain, because the main thread soon reaches something the helper's work could affect and has to wait. Those wait points are now measured one by one (a moving collision object's script, Wander's weapon, message allocation, other objects' animation events, the next character's hand-over); the next round's plan targets them. An attempt to delay the characters' animation events to the end of the helper's work was not exact and stays off. No crash in 600 s runs or loading the save from the console's memory card.
